title: Maximum Quantum-over-Classical Speedup Gap in Symmetric Cryptanalysis
summary: Offline-Simon appears limited to a 2.5 gap, while a cubic separation seems achievable but remains unrealized for cryptographically interesting problems; the maximum attainable gap is unknown.

formal_statement.body: For symmetric cryptanalytic attacks in the classical-query model, determine the largest possible quantum-over-classical speedup gap. The offline-Simon algorithm does not seem capable of producing a gap greater than 2.5, while a cubic separation appears achievable but has not been obtained for problems of cryptographic interest. The unresolved task is to determine the maximum attainable gap under these conditions. (S1)

scope.domain: Quantum and classical query complexity of attacks on symmetric cryptographic schemes.
parameters: quantum-over-classical speedup gap, the quantity to maximize
2.5, the apparent limit for the offline-Simon algorithm
cubic separation, an apparently achievable but not yet obtained gap for cryptographically interesting problems
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the maximum attainable quantum-over-classical speedup gap under the stated conditions.

citations.label: Beyond quadratic speedups in quantum attacks on symmetric schemes

progress.summary: The paper presents increasing the gap as its most obvious open question. It reports that offline-Simon does not seem to exceed 2.5, while a cubic separation seems achievable but was not obtained for a problem of cryptographic interest.
citation_labels: Xavier Bonnetain et al., Beyond quadratic speedups in quantum attacks on symmetric schemes
